decisions.decision: Scope is everything: 13 plugins, 71 unique skills, 21 plugin agents, 4 canvases, 37 repo skills, 50 repo agents, 82 repo prompts, 1 hook, and 3 MCP servers
decisions.why: The reader should never have to leave the book to discover a tool, including the repo's own Spec Kit and WinUI assets
decisions.rejected: Plugins-only scope, which would hide the 37 repo skills and 50 repo agents that do most of the daily work

decisions.decision: Organization is dual: job-to-be-done category chapters plus a complete alphabetical index by source
decisions.why: Categorization is an editorial judgment that will not match every reader's mental model, so the source index guarantees nothing is unreachable
decisions.rejected: Category-only, which hides any entry whose category guess is wrong; source-only, which reproduces the original discovery problem

decisions.decision: Depth is deep for every entry: purpose, use cases, prerequisites, boundaries, and prompt examples
decisions.why: The audience is team onboarding, and a one-line listing leaves the reader exactly where they started
decisions.rejected: Quick-reference tables, which are cheaper to maintain but do not teach invocation

decisions.decision: Static HTML with a read-only drift-check script rather than a full generator
decisions.why: Editorial prose cannot be generated, but staleness can be detected, so the script reports missing, stale, and version-changed entries plus available updates without touching files
decisions.rejected: A full generator, which would produce accurate inventory and lifeless prose; no script at all, which lets the book rot silently

decisions.decision: Light editorial theme only, accent steel blue #1F4E79, with no dark mode
decisions.why: A single palette keeps print output correct by construction and removes an entire class of contrast bugs
decisions.rejected: A theme toggle, which would require print-specific overrides to remain correct

decisions.decision: All assets embedded locally with zero external network requests
decisions.why: The book must render offline and print reliably on a machine with no internet access
decisions.rejected: CDN-hosted fonts or stylesheets, which break offline and print unpredictably

decisions.decision: Print output is US Letter with a cover page, contents page, and one chapter per page break
decisions.why: The requirement is a physical book, so pagination is a first-class feature rather than a stylesheet afterthought
decisions.rejected: Screen-first layout with minimal print rules, which clips wide tables

decisions.decision: Duplicate skill names are documented once with all sources named
decisions.why: csharp-nunit ships in both csharp-dotnet-development and testing-automation, and double-counting would inflate the coverage claim to 72
decisions.rejected: Rendering two indistinguishable entries, which misleads the reader into thinking they differ

concerns: At deep depth across 282 entries the series is likely 25-40 printed pages; category assignment becomes the main editorial risk
Four plugins ship only a canvas, so their chapters must document a surface rather than a skill list
The check script must stay strictly read-only and still report version deltas as actionable updates
last_action: Specification authored from a two-round clarification of scope, structure, depth, theme, and generation strategy.
